identity.title: On the Limits of LLM Adaptability: Impact of Model-Internalized Priors on Annotation Task Performance

problem.claim: The paper investigates how model-internalized priors interact with user instructions in zero-shot annotation and LLM-as-a-judge tasks, focusing on familiarity, prompt-based error correction, and susceptibility to misaligned definitions.

contributions.claim: Introduces Definition-Specific Familiarity (DSF), a measure of alignment between a model’s internal concept and the task definition.
Reports that prompt-based correction is limited: nearly two-thirds of zero-shot toxicity-detection errors resist correction, with a 34.8% rescue rate.
Reports that, after controlling for dataset-level confounds, DSF is positively associated with performance, whereas three text-level memorization metrics are not.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present DSF as a new measure centered on definition-specific alignment rather than text-level memorization.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report a 34.8% overall rescue rate for initially incorrect predictions after prompting across toxicity datasets and dense and mixture-of-experts models.
The authors report that high-confidence errors are especially resistant to correction.

The authors report a partial correlation of +0.41 between DSF and performance after controlling for dataset-level confounds; ROUGE-L, BERTScore, and embedding cosine similarity show no positive association.

narrative_sequence.summary: Frames reliability as dependent on interaction between internalized priors and user instructions.
Defines three investigation dimensions: familiarity, decision stickiness, and response to misaligned task definitions.
Reports resistant zero-shot errors, particularly high-confidence errors, and unchanged confidence under misaligned definitions.
Introduces DSF and reports its positive performance association relative to non-predictive memorization metrics, emphasizing definition alignment.

source_observation.claim: The abstract separates definition-specific familiarity from text-level memorization and reports different associations with performance.

lessons.interpretation: This framing can distinguish conceptual alignment from surface or data similarity when explaining model behavior.
lessons.application: Define and test a task-definition alignment measure alongside memorization proxies when studying annotation performance.
lessons.exception: This move may be unsuitable when the task has no stable, explicit definition or when alignment cannot be operationalized.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify dataset sizes, model identities, prompting protocols, or uncertainty/significance information for the reported associations.
The operational construction and validation of DSF are not described.
The abstract does not establish whether the reported patterns generalize beyond toxicity detection or the listed domains.
